To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the NHS needs to put the patient first, get smart, get systems working and get the culture right.
the English NHS is in many respects a caring and compassionate organisation but is struggling to achieve consistently good quality of care.
‘The NHS has a strong culture that values patient care, but is hampered by a lack of clarity about goals and priorities, poor systems and a fragmented institutional environment’.
In summary, our research is concerned with
what it takes for the NHS to be the best it can be.
the ‘softer side’ of quality and safety.
the culture of care, the culture of improvement and the culture of the organisation.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the NHS has a culture of caring, but it is inconsistent and variable.
the English NHS has many strengths, and many weaknesses.
‘the NHS is not perfect but is getting better’.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the NHS is an institution that is trying to do the right thing, but is struggling to get it right.
the NHS has a good culture and a poor one at the same time, and that the two are related.
the English National Health System is a caring system with caring people, but the system needs to be improved in many ways to achieve the best quality of health care.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the quality of patient care is not a matter of luck or chance; it can be achieved and sustained through a clear focus on the needs of the patient and on the people who provide care.
the NHS has a wealth of talent and innovation, but that the NHS needs to be more effective at harnessing this to achieve the best possible care for patients.
the quality and safety of care is not a technical problem but an issue of culture.
